newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - New York ADRs rise in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - New York ADRs rise in quiet trading.

text.p: Shares in foreign companies largely rose on Monday, with Sweden's LM Ericsson Telephone Corp off slightly, traders said.
American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) for Latin American companies were helped by rising U.S. markets.
The Latin American ADRs are "really being driven by the local markets, which in turn all seem to be driven by the United States," one trader said.
Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian state telecommunications company Telebras was off 1/4 to 80-5/8 with the expiration of options on Monday.
Mexican bottler Coca-Cola FEMSA SA was up 3/8 to 25-1/8 after Kleinwort Benson raised its rating to buy from hold and set a year-end price target of $30.
Indonesian petrochemical company PT Tri Polyta Indonesia was leading New York Stock Exchange shares in terms of percentage gain.
It rose one point, or 14.55 percent, to 7-7/8 on trade of 153,400 shares in the early afternoon. Traders and analysts speculated the rise reflected a recent boost in the stock price in Jakarta.

Ericsson was off 3/8 to 28-1/8 on volume of 1.3 million shares. The dip came despite news the company had joined forces with the United States' Lockheed Martin Corp to offer Airborne Early Warning and Control systems.
"The real question is the mobile telephone market," one trader said. "While this deal on the surface is positive, the focus is still on ... the mobile phone market."
Among a selected 441 ADRs 133 advanced and 142 declined. Volume was 30.39 million shares.
